eval.title: Stock Analysis Cheniere LNG Stock - A Bet on Asia (LNG Demand to Double)

call.headline_quote: cheniere looks like a good bet on long-term us lng prices

base_metric.name: fcf_per_share
base_metric.quote: if i estimate cash flows free cash flows all in and those cash flows that are used to lower the debt as those cash flows arise

scenarios.name: best
scenarios.quote: this company could be debt-free by 2030 which should leave 4.3 billion in cash flows as free cash flows to be paid out as dividends from 2030 onward

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: assuming a 5 required yield if the lng market outlook remains good then you can price this as a bond five percent dividend then the market valuation would be 70 billion

scenarios.name: worst
scenarios.quote: i have given it a 75 chance that it works out as planned and 25 chance that it doesn't work out as planned

reasons.claim: If debt is paid down and cash flows are priced as a bond-like 5% yield, the combined market cap could re-rate from 30 billion to 70-100 billion, giving a large annualized return.
reasons.quote: if it goes to 70 billion for the whole company from the current 30 billion combining the partners and cheniere the corporation that would give you a 14 14.5 yearly return

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: target market cap, expected return

reasons.claim: Cheniere's debt load is huge relative to equity, creating refinancing risk and stock volatility whenever concerns rise.
reasons.quote: long-term net debt is 31 30.8 billion that is a lot and total assets are 45.8 billion equities just 422 million that's that to equity of about 80

reasons.claim: 85% of future production is under long-term contracts, giving safety and stable cash flows regardless of commodity swings.
reasons.quote: 85 of future production is contracted which gives safety for the company

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: contracted production

reasons.claim: US LNG producers sit high on the global cost curve, so if demand disappoints or competitors like Russia and Shell increase output, US producers could be squeezed out over the long term.
reasons.quote: u.s producers are really on the high end end on that cost curve so when you're on high end any changes in demand that are different than expected might be very detrimental for you

reasons.claim: As investing spend subsides and free cash flow ramps up, it will be used to pay down debt and raise dividends, which typically lifts the stock price.
reasons.quote: that is expected to subdue over the next year two years which should lead into high cash flows high positive cash flows that will be used to lower the debt and increase dividends and as we all know when dividends go up so does the stock price

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: investing cash outflow
